2609.28575.title: TWIST: A Proposed Benchmark for Intervention Quality in Conversational Memory, with a Human-Validated Draft-Alignment
2609.28575.paper_summary: Long-conversation memory benchmarks increasingly test recall and prompted knowledge updates, and recent work studies evolving user beliefs and memory state. TWIST is a proposed benchmark suite for a complementary, unmeasured property: intervention quality -- whether a deployed memory system, exercised through its own ingest/recall/vet surface, acts correctly at belief change points. Four tracks cover unprompted tension detection, vetting outgoing drafts against the record, answering with current beliefs while preserving supersession history, and governing sensitive recall. The suite extends LoCoMo's corpora and harness, pairing every detect/block metric with a matched do-not-over-detect control: surface-matched hard negatives price false intervention, so no track can be gamed by flagging everything. The benchmark itself is validated first: independent, gold-blind double annotation with adjudication, judge decoy calibration, and a separability audit. On the human-validated Track B v1.0 key (161 items, post-adjudication kappa = 0.85), no tested configuration simultaneously achieves high contradiction recall, high hard-negative specificity, and high attribution: flat-RAG baselines detect 0.76-0.97 of true contradictions but falsely flag 16-43% of surface-matched safe drafts depending on backend, while a deployed coherence-oriented system almost never over-flags (0.98-1.00 specificity) yet catches 42% of true contradictions -- a trade-off no recall-only score can see. A 13-configuration baseline ladder localizes causes: every gold contradiction is detectable from its evidence alone (recall 1.000), calibrated models nearly solve the track given the full transcript -- consistent with substantial retrieval-coverage gaps -- and draft-only floors reveal model-dependent style priors. A system's TWIST profile, beside its recall score, measures whether memory knows when to intervene and when not to.
2609.28575.paper_summary_zh: 長期對話記憶基準越來越多地測試回憶和提示知識更新，而最近的研究則探討了用戶信念和記憶狀態的演變。TWIST是一個提出的基準套件，用於補充一個未被測量的屬性：介入質量——即部署的記憶系統是否在信念變更點正確運作，通過其自身的攝取/回憶/驗證界面進行操作。四個軌道涵蓋了未提示的緊張檢測、對照記錄審核發出的草稿、在保留取代歷史的同時用當前信念回答，以及管理敏感回憶。該套件擴展了LoCoMo的語料庫和工具，將每個檢測/阻止指標與匹配的不要過度檢測控制配對：表面匹配的硬負樣本對虛假介入的代價，因此沒有任何軌道可以通過標記所有內容來操縱。基準本身首先得到驗證：獨立的金盲雙重標註與裁決、評審誘餌校準和可分離性審核。在經人類驗證的Track B v1.0關鍵（161項目，裁決後kappa = 0.85）中，沒有測試配置同時實現高矛盾回憶、高硬負樣本特異性和高歸因：平坦的RAG基線檢測到0.76-0.97的真實矛盾，但根據後端錯誤標記16-43%的表面匹配安全草稿，而一個部署的以一致性為導向的系統幾乎從不過度標記（0.98-1.00特異性），卻捕捉到42%的真實矛盾——這是一種任何僅回憶分數無法看到的權衡。一個13配置的基線梯度定位原因：每個金矛盾都可以僅從其證據中檢測到（回憶1.000），經過校準的模型幾乎解決了給定完整抄本的軌道——與實質性檢索覆蓋缺口一致——而僅草稿的底線揭示了模型依賴的風格先驗。一個系統的TWIST檔案，除了其回憶分數外，還衡量記憶是否知道何時介入以及何時不介入。
